Marker-assisted backcrossing and gene pyramiding

Source: R/backcross.R
backcross_program.Rd

Simulates introgressing one or more target genes from a donor into a recurrent parent (RP) by marker-assisted backcrossing, then fixing them by selfing. Every argument can be tuned, so the classic design questions (how many plants per generation, how many backcross generations, how close the flanking markers should be, how dense the background markers, and whether to introgress several genes together or in parallel streams) become one call to tune_grid() or tune_bayes().

Usage

backcross_program(..., targets = data.frame(chr = 1, pos = 50))

Arguments

...

Arguments to set or tune: strategy, bc_generations, n_plants, n_keep, flank_cM, bg_spacing, bg_from, fix_plants, pyramid_plants, n_chromosomes, chromosome_length, plant_cost, datapoint_cost, generations_per_year.

targets

Data frame with columns chr and pos (cM): where the target genes are.

Value

A backcross_program spec.

Selection in each backcross generation

Each generation grows n_plants plants and selects in three stages, as in Hospital and Charcosset (1997) and Frisch et al. (1999):

  1. Foreground: plants carrying the donor allele at every target, read from a diagnostic marker on each gene.

  2. Recombinant: among carriers, those with the most recombinant flanking markers, placed flank_cM on each side of each target. This limits linkage drag. Use flank_cM = Inf to skip this stage.

  3. Background: from generation bg_from on, the remaining plants are ranked by the share of RP alleles at markers every bg_spacing cM. Use bg_spacing = Inf to skip it.

The best n_keep plants are backcrossed to the RP. After bc_generations, the best plant is selfed, fix_plants progeny are grown, and a plant homozygous for every target is kept, with ties broken by background.

Several targets

With more than one target, strategy = "simultaneous" backcrosses all of them together, selecting carriers of every target each generation. strategy = "parallel" follows Peng et al. (2014a, b). Each target gets its own backcross stream of n_plants per generation, and each conversion is fixed by selfing. The conversions are then pyramided by crossing them in pairs, then crossing those hybrids, and so on (a symmetric schedule, as in Ishii and Yonezawa, 2007). Each crossing step grows pyramid_plants and keeps the plant carrying every target with the best background. A final selfing fixes the pyramid.

Outcomes

  • success: 1 if the final plant is homozygous for the donor allele at every target, else 0.

  • rp_recovery: percent of the final plant's genome from the RP.

  • donor_cM: donor genome left, in cM per haploid genome.

  • linkage_drag: mean length in cM of the donor segment around each target.

  • generations and years: crossing and selfing generations, and years at generations_per_year. Parallel streams run at the same time.

  • plants, datapoints (marker data points) and cost.

References

Hospital F, Charcosset A (1997) Marker-assisted introgression of quantitative trait loci. Genetics 147:1469-1485. doi:10.1093/genetics/147.3.1469

Frisch M, Bohn M, Melchinger AE (1999) Comparison of selection strategies for marker-assisted backcrossing of a gene. Crop Science 39:1295-1301.

Hospital F (2001) Size of donor chromosome segments around introgressed loci and reduction of linkage drag in marker-assisted backcross programs. Genetics 158:1363-1379. doi:10.1093/genetics/158.3.1363

Peng T, Sun X, Mumm RH (2014a) Optimized breeding strategies for multiple trait integration: I. Minimizing linkage drag in single event introgression. Molecular Breeding 33:89-104. doi:10.1007/s11032-013-9936-7

Peng T, Sun X, Mumm RH (2014b) Optimized breeding strategies for multiple trait integration: II. Process efficiency in event pyramiding and trait fixation. Molecular Breeding 33:105-115. doi:10.1007/s11032-013-9937-6

Ishii T, Yonezawa K (2007) Optimization of the marker-based procedures for pyramiding genes from multiple donor lines: I. Schedule of crossing between the donor lines. Crop Science 47:537-546.

Examples

spec <- backcross_program(n_plants = tune(), flank_cM = tune(), n_chromosomes = 5)
res <- tune_grid(spec, sim_replicates(5), grid = expand.grid(n_plants = c(50, 150), flank_cM = c(5, 20)))
collect_metrics(res, type = "wide")
#> # A tibble: 4 × 18
#>   n_plants flank_cM success success_se rp_recovery rp_recovery_se linkage_drag
#>      <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>      <dbl>       <dbl>          <dbl>        <dbl>
#> 1       50        5       1          0        98.8          0.191          3.4
#> 2      150        5       1          0        98.6          0.265          5  
#> 3       50       20       1          0        98.0          0.463          9.8
#> 4      150       20       1          0        97.7          0.340         12.4
#> # ℹ 11 more variables: linkage_drag_se <dbl>, years <dbl>, years_se <dbl>,
#> #   plants <dbl>, plants_se <dbl>, datapoints <dbl>, datapoints_se <dbl>,
#> #   cost <dbl>, cost_se <dbl>, n <int>, .config <chr>
